contagion_stress_scenario.text: `sector_stress_scenario` answers "what is my P&L if each sector takes a given shock?" You give it each sector's exposure (`sector_exposures`) and shock (`sector_shocks`), and it sums exposure times shock across sectors, so total P&L is exactly the sum of the per-sector P&L. `contagion_stress_scenario` answers a different question: "how does an initial shock spread through a network of linked nodes?" It takes an `initial_shock`, a `contagion_matrix` of spillover coefficients, and a number of `rounds`, and it adds up the shock plus its successive spillovers. In short, the first applies shocks you specify directly to each sector, while the second works out how a shock travels between connected nodes. The second returns a cumulative shock, not a P&L figure.

explain.text: `sector_stress_scenario` (Sector Stress Scenario) runs a sector-level stress test on a portfolio. You give it `sector_exposures`, the currency P&L per unit move for each sector, and `sector_shocks`, the shock applied to each sector. It multiplies each sector's exposure by its shock and sums the results, so total P&L is the exact sum of the per-sector P&L. You can pass `sector_names` to label the sectors; otherwise they default to `sector_0`, and so on.

when.text:
Use Sector Stress Scenario (`sector_stress_scenario`) when you want to see how a shock to specific sectors would hit a portfolio:

- You know your net exposure per sector, expressed as currency P&L per unit move (`sector_exposures`), and want to apply a shock to each one (`sector_shocks`).
- You want a total P&L that is exactly the sum of the per-sector P&L, so you can see which sectors drive the outcome.
- You want to run a sector-level what-if, such as a different shock for each sector, with optional labels via `sector_names`.
- You want a simple, transparent calculation: each sector's exposure times its shock, then added up.

If you instead need to push an initial shock through a spillover network, `contagion_stress_scenario` is listed as propagating an initial shock through a contagion (spillover) network.
